solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ought, with hesitation, to take responsibility

parts.note: ought means should, as in 'you ought to go'
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone, after some hemming and hawing, agrees they ought to accept the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to accept responsibility for it, carrying it as if on one's back.

parts.note: read as a railway running beneath a city, or a passage beneath a road for walkers

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word means a tunnel for walking under a busy road; in the US it is the underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: In America this is the metro railway; in Britain it is a pedestrian tunnel under a road.

clue.text: Too much rudder admitted first watch to master

parts.note: over means excessive, as in 'over the top'

indicators.note: the first letter of watch is the piece that is taken in

parts.note: the helm is the tiller or wheel that steers a boat

explanation.surface: A ship's officer finds the helm too heavy before the first watch takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted first' means the rudder takes the watch's initial in at its front, not somewhere in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm an opponent is to overpower and so master them completely.

definitions.meaning: enjoys or values something, as in 'she appreciates good food'
used as a verb, values highly

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who appreciates or prizes a thing is fond of it, a plain synonym for both senses.

parts.note: read not as an emergency telephone link but as an imaginary line on the globe where the climate is hot

explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary circle round the middle of the earth runs through the tropics, the hottest region.

parts.note: a spitfire is a fiery, quarrelsome person, as is a shrew

explanation.surface: A Second World War fighter plane takes to the air during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' and 'spitfire' suggest the RAF fighter plane; 'Fly' is in fact the British slang adjective meaning sharp or knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is informal British slang for astute and knowing, a synonym of quick-witted.

parts.note: read not as making a stylish impression but as putting a short horizontal punctuation mark into a word

explanation.definitionFit: To join or split words with a short punctuation stroke is to insert a dash-like mark between them.

clue.text: Not an all-American name for a girl

indicators.note: not an entire word: only a run of letters from inside the compound is wanted

explanation.surface: A girl's name that does not sound wholly American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not an' all-American name tells you to take only part of the word ALL-AMERICAN, the letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a familiar female first name, so it is a name for a girl.

definitions.meaning: to scatter or go in different directions, as a crowd does
to spread out what was gathered densely together

explanation.definitionFit: A crowd that disperses moves off, and scattering something dense breaks up its concentration.

clue.text: Suffers divorce and goes to pieces

definitions.meaning: a couple ending their marriage separates for good

explanation.definitionFit: A couple who separate are said to split up, and something shattering likewise falls apart into fragments.

definitions.meaning: the gymnastic stretch with legs flat on the floor in opposite directions

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for departing quickly, and also the name of the floor stretch with legs spread fully apart.

parts.note: on a compass, 180 degrees is due south, S
'between 180 and 270' is read as 180 to 270, so this word supplies TO
on a compass, 270 degrees is due west, W

explanation.surface: A navigator lists a storage location by its compass bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass sector between 180 and 270 degrees runs from south to west, read as S TO W.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow something is to pack it away, a plain synonym for storing it.

clue.text: Alternately, Warsaw's also in a former state

indicators.note: only every other letter of the following words is used, starting with the second

parts.note: the backwards run inside these words is a coincidence; the setter's device is the alternate letters

explanation.surface: A comment that Poland's capital also once belonged to some earlier state.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something left unchanged, exactly as it was before, so in its earlier condition.

parts.note: a title is a legal right to something, as in title to land
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: An employer tells a new servant he is entitled to begin his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start work' reads as a verb phrase, but it is a noun: the opening leaf of a book or other work.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf naming a book sits at its very beginning, so it is the start of a written work.

clue.text: Name and number for a subordinate

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs, here the old anaesthetic gas

explanation.surface: A form asks for a junior employee's name and staff number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that makes you numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower, so it describes something placed beneath and subordinate in position.

clue.text: Deliberate exaggeration may possibly be her ploy

indicators.note: suggests the letters of the following words could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's overstatement might just be her tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is the rhetorical term for intentional overstatement used for effect.

clue.text: From this raw spirits are made

indicators.note: the answer is fashioned out of the raw material named, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Instructions for distilling spirits from raw ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' looks like alcohol made from raw materials; it means ghosts. 'are made' turns THIS RAW into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wraiths are ghostly apparitions, the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Advocates getting money to create large food store

indicators.note: the money word gets the lawyers into itself, holding them inside

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
the Bar is the collective name for barristers, so the Bar means advocates

explanation.surface: Lawyers make money to build a big warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BAR (barristers collectively) goes inside TIN, British slang for cash. A tithe barn stored the tenth of farm produce paid to the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn was a large farm building where crops paid as church dues were stored.

definitions.meaning: taking up a cause or idea as one's own

explanation.definitionFit: One may espouse a spouse in wedlock or espouse a cause by embracing it.

clue.text: Showing unusual promise, he may take part for money

definitions.text: he may take part for money

indicators.note: unusual signals that the following word appears in an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: A youngster showing remarkable talent might play in return for pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-professional plays sport partly for pay while holding another job.

clue.text: Drive away uphill, with exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: in a down entry, going uphill means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: shoo means to drive away an animal or pest

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls off up a hill to cries of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Oohs are sounds people make when amazed or delighted, interjections of wonder.

clue.text: Slim elves play around the square

indicators.note: the jumbled elves go around the square, holding it inside
the elves at play move about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler, so the square is T

explanation.surface: Lean little elves frolic about the village square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' turns ELVES into SVELE, and 'around' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and graceful, a synonym of slim.

clue.text: C-in-C starts to drink, gets more merry

parts.note: to begin drinking is to sup, take a mouthful

indicators.note: merry suggests the following word is tipsy and so jumbled

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief takes to the bottle and gets jollier.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall command, like a commander-in-chief.

clue.text: Do some asset stripping to run church

parts.note: flee means run away
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A corporate raider runs off to a church after stripping a company's assets.
explanation.walkthrough: To fleece is both to cheat someone of money and literally to strip a sheep of its wool.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them, stripping them of their assets.

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A fresh professional takes the championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PRO HE WINS. 'title' looks like a sports championship; it is the legal sense, the right to property.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal title to property is the right of possession, that is, being its owner in law.

definitions.meaning: the saying 'as hard as' a certain set of metal pins
the horny coverings at the ends of the toes

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says 'hard as nails', and toenails grow at the tips of the toes.

definitions.meaning: the long rolling motion of the sea
to expand or increase in size

explanation.definitionFit: The rolling sea is called the swell, and to swell is to grow larger.

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone is a little subdued and flushed with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap or fragment, so a small bit of something.

parts.note: AB is the abbreviation for an able-bodied seaman, so a man with AB rank is a seafarer

explanation.walkthrough: AB stands for able-bodied seaman, a basic rank in the British navy.
explanation.definitionFit: An able seaman, abbreviated AB, is a rating in the navy, a mariner.

definitions.meaning: read playfully as ..., to take the creases out

explanation.definitionFit: To decrease is to diminish, and split as de-crease it means taking out creases.

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bar snack of salted nuts kept coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the snack but means mad, so SALTED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lasted went on, continuing over time.

parts.note: a con man, shortened to con
dense means stupid

explanation.surface: A dim-witted crook is told to focus.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a liquid or text is to make it more compact, that is to concentrate it.
